topic: Modes of Reproduction in Flowering and Non-Flowering Plants
key_concepts: Flowering plants reproduce sexually through pollination and fertilization.
Non-flowering plants like ferns and mosses reproduce with spores.
Ferns have fronds, fiddleheads, and sori that release spores.
Mosses produce spore cases that burst and release spores onto moist ground.
A pollen tube grows from a pollen grain on the stigma down the style to the ovary.
Fertilization occurs when a sperm cell unites with an egg cell in the ovule.

Seeds contain a seed coat, hilum, embryo, and cotyledon or cotyledons.
Mongo is a dicot with two cotyledons; corn is a monocot with one cotyledon.
Mosses and ferns can reproduce both sexually and asexually.
Cotyledons nourish the young plant until leaves can make food.
Successful fertilization leads to a swollen ovary, wilted petals, and seed formation.
